messages:
customer-admin: Hey team — our on‑prem Redwood Private deploy in our VPC started failing to pull model shards after a firewall change. Downloads hit TLS / cert verify errors in the downloader process. Can we get a minimal egress allowlist (hosts + ports) so we can update the perimeter and retest?

mira: Sorry you're hitting this — we can help. Do you have a short curl/openssl trace from one of the hosts that fails? Also: are you doing TLS inspection (corporate MITM) or a forward proxy? That changes recommendations.

customer-admin: We're behind a corporate forward proxy that can do TLS interception. Attaching the error from the model pull job (redacted):

```
2026-01-15T09:12:03Z downloader error: GET https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/large/manifest -> dial tcp 54.23.11.45:443: EOF
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to model-registry.redwood.ai:443 
```

And curl -v from the same host:

```
$ curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
*   Trying 54.23.11.45:443...
* Connected to model-registry.redwood.ai (54.23.11.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* server certificate verification failed. CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt CRLfile: none
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

We also ran: `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -showcerts` and it prints a cert chain ending in an intermediate we don't trust (corporate MITM replaces cert).

jordan: Thanks for the traces. Two quick things before we hand off a list: 1) if your proxy performs TLS termination/re-signing, the easiest path is to import your proxy CA into the Private deployment's JVM/OS truststore so the downloader trusts the re-signed certs. Otherwise you need to ensure direct TLS passthrough for the hostnames below. 2) for model shards we rely on a mix of our control plane endpoints and object storage endpoints (S3/compatible).

jordan: Here's a minimal host/port allowlist we recommend for on‑prem deployments to allow model pulls, auth, and telemetry (ports: 443 unless noted):

```
- model-registry.redwood.ai            # model manifest & shard coordination (443)
- registry-geo.redwood.ai             # geo/edge model metadata (443)
- models-cache.redwood.ai             # CDN/edge caching hosts (443)
- auth.redwood-inference.com          # auth/token issuance (443)
- telemetry-ingest.redwood.ai         # runtime telemetry/metrics (443)
- packages.pypi.org                   # pip installs for runtime deps (443)
- files.debian.org                    # apt deps (443)
- s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com          # model shard object storage (443)
- kms.redwood-inference.com           # key exchange / KMS (443)
- ocsp.globalsign.com                 # OCSP stapling checks (80/443) — ensure OCSP not blocked
```

jordan: If your perimeter only allows IP/CIDR rules, common IP ranges we use for model/object storage and registry services (subject to change) are: "54.16.0.0/12", "52.216.0.0/15", and AWS S3 ranges for us-west-2. NOTE: IP-based allowlists are brittle because CDNs and cloud ranges change. Hostname allowlist + proxy passthrough is preferred.

mira: A few operational notes / gotchas we've seen:
- If TLS inspection is enabled, ensure the proxy preserves the original SNI header. Our SDK uses SNI to route to edge replicas; if SNI is removed it can route incorrectly and handshake will fail.
- Allow outbound DNS (UDP/53 and TCP/53) to resolve the hostnames. Blocked DNS leads to failures that show up as timeouts, not TLS errors.
- Allow HTTP (port 80) egress to our telemetry and Let's Encrypt / OCSP endpoints for AIA/OCSP fetching.
- For quick testing: on a host in your VPC run `curl -vk --resolve model-registry.redwood.ai:443:54.23.11.45 https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health` to bypass DNS and surface TLS issues.

customer-admin: Helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups: can you confirm whether model download clients validate OCSP/CRL by default? We were seeing connection drops mid-download. Also — do you publish a short-lived IP list we can use for emergencies?

jordan: Our downloader will validate certificate chains and accept stapled OCSP responses. If your proxy strips stapled OCSP the downloader will fall back to an AIA fetch which requires outbound HTTP to the CA endpoints (hence ocsp.globalsign.com above). Mid-download drops are usually: proxy idle timeout or MTU issues on the path to S3. If downloads start and then TCP reset, please share a packet capture and we can look for RSTs.

jordan: For emergency/temporary network rules we can provide a time-limited list of IPs for the next 7 days if you open a support ticket and give us the account/org id. Long term — hostname allowlist + truststore update (to trust your proxy CA) is the robust solution.

mira: I'll open a ticket with infra to give you the temporary IPs. In parallel, please run these repro steps on one failing host and paste the outputs here:
1) `curl -vk https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health`
2) `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -status` (shows OCSP status)
3) `traceroute -n model-registry.redwood.ai`
4) tcpdump (30s) on egress interface filtering port 443: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/egress.pcap`

ops-bot: Support ticket #SUP-2026-438 opened for customer ACME Corp — please attach pcap and account id.

customer-admin: Will do, attaching the pcap and traceroute shortly. Thanks for the quick triage! :pray:
